title: Regional fallback topology schema and verification checklist
summary: Lab-style notes that define a compact JSON/YAML schema for region-aware routing + fallback topologies, an automated validation surface for config linting and unit tests, and a practical canary/checklist sequence for safe rollout with telemetry gating.
body:
Purpose
This doc captures a minimal, opinionated schema for routing policies that include region topology, primary/secondary model variants, and explicit fallback behavior. It also records the validation checks and a verification checklist used during canary and progressive rollout. Target audience: platform engineers and SREs who own control-plane rollout automation.

Problem statement / context
- We need deterministic behavior when a region is impaired: explicit fallback targets, throttling and degraded-capacity policies, and a validation surface that prevents accidental global traffic overrides.
- Current configs are ad hoc (per-customer overrides live in multiple places) — we want a single canonical schema + linters + unit tests to make automated rollouts safer.

Design goals (practical)
- Declarative, small surface area: routing rules should express source, priority list of targets, and per-target constraints (capacity, max-rps, latency-slo).
- Fail explicitly: never rely on implicit global defaults; every rule must include an ordered fallback list.
- Safe-by-default deploys: new rules start with 0% traffic unless explicitly canaried/pinned.
- Machine-validated: schema checks + semantic validators + integration smoke tests before promotion.

Canonical schema (YAML-like example)
Note: keep this compact. The actual control plane implements equivalent JSON schema + type checks.

---
kind: RoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: hosted-text-default
  version: v1.1
  created_by: aisha.kapoor@redwood.com
spec:
  description: "Default text generation route for hosted API in eu/us regions"
  sources:
    - cluster: api-gateway
  rules:
    - id: primary-eu
      priority: 10
      targets:
        - region: eu-west-1
          model_variant: redwood-gamma-13b-q4
          max_rps: 1200
          latency_slo_ms: 200
          degrade_policy: throttle_percent: 30
        - region: eu-central-1
          model_variant: redwood-gamma-13b-q4
          max_rps: 600
          latency_slo_ms: 280
      fallback:
        - region: global-readonly
          model_variant: redwood-gamma-13b-cpu
    - id: fallback-global
      priority: 100
      targets:
        - region: global-readonly
          model_variant: redwood-gamma-13b-cpu
          max_rps: 300
          latency_slo_ms: 600
  rollout_policy:
    initial_percent: 0
    canary_steps:
      - percent: 1
        duration_minutes: 30
      - percent: 10
        duration_minutes: 60
      - percent: 50
        duration_minutes: 120
    final_percent: 100
    fail_fast_on:
      - metric: error_rate
        operator: gt
        threshold: 0.02
      - metric: p95_latency_ms
        operator: gt
        threshold: 2.0
---

Validation surfaces
We split checks into three layers: schema (syntactic), semantic, and integration/smoke.

1) Schema checks (JSON Schema / openapi-style)
- Required fields: kind, metadata.name, spec.rules (non-empty), spec.rollout_policy.initial_percent present.
- Field types and ranges: priority integer >=0, max_rps non-negative integer, latency_slo_ms positive integer.
- No empty fallback arrays: spec.rules[].fallback must be non-empty unless the rule has a single global target and is explicitly marked immutable.

2) Semantic validators (control-plane hooks, run asynchronously in CI)
- Region compatibility: ensure model_variant listed is available in the target region (lookup table).
- Resource caps: per-tenant and per-region capacity quotas must not be exceeded by sum(max_rps) of active rules.
- Circular fallback detection: fallbacks must not form cycles across rules (detect graph cycles).
- Priority consistency: lower priority number is higher precedence; ensure there are no duplicate priority values for the same source cluster unless tie-break strategy is present.

3) Integration/smoke tests (run in ephemeral test harness)
- Synthetic traffic generator routes to configured source and asserts the observed target region matches the top-priority available target given a simulated region outage.
- Latency injection tests: simulate high-latency at the primary region and assert fallback activates per degrade_policy threshold.
- Chaos scenario: detaching a region from the backend stack should trigger routing to fallback and emit specific telemetry events.

Automated lint rules (examples)
- RULE001: name must be kebab-case and <= 48 chars
- RULE002: rollout_policy.initial_percent must be present and between 0 and 100
- RULE003: each rule MUST include fallback list unless opt_out: true and opt_out_reason provided
- RULE004: any model_variant referenced must exist in the onboarded-models registry (checked by CI)
- RULE005: no priority collisions for same source cluster

Sample unit tests to add to control-plane repo
- test_schema_rejects_missing_fallback()
- test_semantic_rejects_unavailable_model_variant()
- test_cycle_detection_on_fallback_graph()
- test_rollout_steps_apply_traffic_deltas_correctly()

Rollout mechanics (checklist for an engineer performing a canary)
Pre-rollout (authoring + CI)
- [ ] Author route file, set rollout_policy.initial_percent: 0
- [ ] Run local linter (platformctl lint route.yaml) and fix all RULExxx failures
- [ ] Push PR referencing PLAT-1953 and include sample smoke harness config
- [ ] CI must run schema + semantic validators; resolve blocking failures

Canary promotion steps (manual guardrails)
- Step 0: Apply config to staging with rollout_policy.initial_percent=100 and run full smoke tests (must pass)
- Step 1: Apply to prod with initial_percent=0 (no traffic) and verify no immediate route changes in metrics dashboards
- Step 2: Start canary: bump to canary step 1 (1%) via control-plane API; wait for duration_minutes and monitor gates
- Step 3: Gates to observe during each step:
    - error_rate (per-route) < 0.5% absolute and < baseline+1% relative
    - p95_latency_ms < configured latency_slo_ms * 1.5
    - CPU/GPU utilization per-region < quota threshold (configured per cluster)
    - anomaly signals from model quality checker: no large divergence in embedding distances or generation length distributions
- Step 4: If gates pass, progress to the next canary step; if any gate triggers fail_fast_on, the control plane should automatically revert to previous percent and notify #plat-routing channel
- Step 5: After reaching final_percent, run 24h night-watch with elevated telemetry retention for the route

Rollback and postmortem triggers
- Automatic rollback triggers: any fail_fast_on metric crossing threshold OR a manual SRE/PM decision. Rollback must restore the previous active config version and annotate the change with the reason.
- Postmortem required if rollback occurred or if cumulative error impact > 0.1% of global requests for 1h.

Diagnostics and runbook excerpts
- Control-plane API endpoints to inspect resolution path: GET /routes/{name}/expanded?source=api-gateway returns computed target selection with priorities and active fallback.
- Debug commands for SRE:
    - platformctl resolve-route hosted-text-default --source api-gateway --simulate-region=eu-west-1
    - platformctl simulate-latency hosted-text-default --target-region=eu-west-1 --latency-ms=450
    - platformctl lint route.yaml --rules RULE001,RULE003
- Telemetry events emitted on failover:
    - event: route.fallback.activated -> fields: route_name, from_region, to_region, reason_code
    - event: route.degrade.throttle_applied -> fields: route_name, target_region, throttle_percent

Open questions / follow-ups
- How to bake model health signals into the gating logic (model quality vs infra health)? Need follow-up meeting with applied-ml to define acceptable signal surface.
- Should we allow dynamic runtime overrides from operations for emergencies? If yes, add an ops-only override namespace with time-bounded TTL and audit hooks.
- Can we auto-suggest fallback targets based on historical latency and capacity instead of requiring explicit lists? Risk: surprises during outage if suggestions are stale.

Appendix: quick JSON Schema sketch (excerpt)
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["kind","metadata","spec"],
  "properties": {
    "kind": {"type": "string"},
    "metadata": {"type": "object"},
    "spec": {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["rules","rollout_policy"],
      "properties": {
        "rules": {"type": "array"},
        "rollout_policy": {"type": "object"}
      }
    }
  }
}

Notes on uniqueness of this doc
- This is intentionally compact and operational: a single-file lab note that ties schema, validation, and a concrete canary checklist together. It is intended to be a living artifact in platform-engineering for quick iteration.

Owner notes
- Next steps: pair with Marcus to add RULE004 check in CI and create the test harness PR. Schedule a 30-minute sync with Applied ML to discuss model-health signals.
